title: RideLink Standing Orders for Recurring Treatment — Level Terms
content:
Recurring treatment trips under Non-Emergency Medical Transportation may be set up as a standing order on some RideLink levels of service. The utilization management terms below state where standing orders are allowed, how long one order lasts at most before renewal, and which treatments qualify.

| Level | Standing orders allowed | Longest order before renewal (months) | Qualifying treatments |
|---|---|---|---|
| RideLink Transit Pass | No | 0 | None |
| RideLink Mileage Reimbursement | No | 0 | None |
| RideLink Ambulatory Sedan | Yes | 6 | Dialysis, chemotherapy, radiation, behavioral health, opioid treatment program |
| RideLink Door-to-Door Assist | Yes | 6 | Dialysis, chemotherapy, radiation, behavioral health, opioid treatment program |
| RideLink Wheelchair Van | Yes | 6 | Dialysis, chemotherapy, radiation, behavioral health, opioid treatment program |
| RideLink Stretcher Van | Yes | 3 | Dialysis, chemotherapy, radiation |

## Points of judgement

- A behavioral health or opioid treatment program schedule qualifies on RideLink Ambulatory Sedan, RideLink Door-to-Door Assist and RideLink Wheelchair Van, but not on RideLink Stretcher Van.
- A standing order on RideLink Stretcher Van lasts at most 3 months; on the other three levels that allow orders, at most 6 months.
- RideLink Transit Pass and RideLink Mileage Reimbursement set up no standing orders.

*Hypothetical case:* a dialysis schedule on RideLink Wheelchair Van starting 1 February may be set up as one standing order lasting no more than 6 months.
